body:
RCanthony001.jpg is not 100% okidoki according to imagemagick:

```text
$ identify -regard-warnings RCanthony001.jpg
RCanthony001.jpg JPEG 640x640 640x640+0+0 8-bit sRGB 104880B 0.000u 0:00.006
identify-im6.q16: Corrupt JPEG data: 63 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9 `RCanthony001.jpg' @ warning/jpeg.c/JPEGWarningHandler/389
```

It fails here, `tj3Decompress8` returns `-1`

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/873833b4a7dcbbf5c264353de4546b66f8ec9132/modules/jpg/image_loader_libjpeg_turbo.cpp#L70-L73

by introducing `print_line(tj3GetErrorStr(tj_instance));` in this block, we can also get: `Corrupt JPEG data: 63 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9`

I tried to make libjpeg-turbo less strict via `tj3Set(tj_instance, TJPARAM_STOPONWARNING, 0);` but to no avail.

Image imports fine when we ignore the `-1` return.

I suppose other applications just ignore extraneous bytes that the parser complains about. So Godot would check `tj3GetErrorCode(tj_instance)` and check for `TJERR_WARNING` then continue. Alternatively, Godot could be strict and print the error message from libjpeg-turbo to console.

My main concern is for applications/games that rely heavily on Importing/loading user images at runtime. Many Godot developers would probably find it trivial to just re-encode the images with ffmpeg, but an end user having an image fail on import, an image that to them is displaying perfectly fine, is a point of frustration and confusion.
Being too strict in the eyes of the end user will be perceived as a flaw/bug of the application/game.
